public_rationale: Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing describes substantial fixed compute obligations and risks to meeting them [e1]. It does not establish substantial nonpayment or definitive repudiation by both Anthropic and OpenAI, or sector-wide demand after such an event [e1]. The conditional forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: The evidence does not establish whether every payment was made.
The referenced $1.3 trillion is not reconciled to contracts, amounts due and payment schedules.
The packet provides no post-trigger demand measurements; the claim specifies no deadline or observation lag.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If Anthropic and OpenAI don't pay their $1.3 trillion in compute bills, AI data center demand will collapse.
conditions: if Anthropic and OpenAI don't pay their compute bills

statement.excerpt: If they aren’t going to pay those $1.3 trillion in compute bills, the jig is up for AI data center demand.

from_speaker: If they aren’t going to pay
the jig is up for AI data center demand
our_interpretation: The antecedent means a substantial failure or definitive refusal by the two companies to meet the referenced compute obligations. It does not mean that all future commitments are already payable.
The plain reading of 'the jig is up' is a broad and sustained collapse in commercially funded AI data center demand, not merely slower growth or a decline at one supplier.
The supplied words do not identify the accounting basis or contractual composition of the $1.3 trillion.
criteria.support_condition: After documented substantial nonpayment or repudiation of the referenced obligations by Anthropic and OpenAI, sector-wide bookings, utilization and related revenues show a broad sustained collapse attributable to the lost demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent is established, comparable sector data show demand remaining substantial and sustained despite the labs' nonpayment. Conditions before the antecedent cannot contradict this forecast.

evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 32, paragraph on minimum purchase and take-or-pay commitments
evidence.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: The filing establishes the existence of fixed obligations and discusses the risk of underused compute. Neither the quoted disclosure nor the reviewed financing passages establish substantial nonpayment by both Anthropic and OpenAI.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contracts, creditor notices, court records or company disclosures establishing substantial nonpayment or definitive repudiation by both labs. Subsequent sector-wide bookings, utilization and realized revenues, including replacement customers, must then establish either a broad sustained collapse attributable to that lost demand or substantial sustained demand despite it.
